name: chess
doc:
CHESS - the rules decide (issue #11, 2026-10-16: reach, down the domain list). A claim about a position is
computed by the Laws of Chess, never judged: the classic mates (fool's, scholar's, smothered, back-rank) SEALED as
checkmate, a king-and-queen stalemate SEALED as stalemate and as not-check, move legality SEALED both ways (a
legal push, an illegal one sealed as illegal, en passant, castling), and the material count. All through
chess.CHESS_VERIFY over the perft-proven move generator. The Laws and the piece values are CITED; the verdicts
are SEALED. Idempotent.

sticks.question: Chess - the rules decide: mate, stalemate, legality, material
sticks.statement: A claim about a chess position is decided by the Laws of Chess applied to the position - computed by the move generator, never judged.
references: F.-A. D. Philidor, Analyse du jeu des Echecs (1749) - the smothered mate

marks.claim: [fool's mate, SEALED] 1.f3 e5 2.g4 Qh4# - White to move is checkmated (sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY). The shortest possible mate: two pawn moves open the diagonal to the king and nothing can interpose.
[scholar's mate, SEALED] 1.e4 e5 2.Bc4 Nc6 3.Qh5 Nf6 4.Qxf7# - Black is checkmated (sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY): the queen on f7 is guarded by the bishop on c4, the king has no flight square.

[the smothered mate, SEALED] King h8, rook g8, pawns g7 h7; a white knight lands on f7 and it is mate (sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY). The king is smothered by its own pieces - Philidor's pattern (1749), the oldest named mate in the literature.
[the back-rank mate, SEALED] King g8 behind its three pawns, a rook arrives on a8: mate (sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY). The pawns that shielded the king are the wall that traps it.

[stalemate, SEALED] Black king h8, white queen f7, white king g6, Black to move: stalemate (sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY). Every square the king could reach is attacked and no other piece exists - no legal move, so the game is drawn (Laws 5.2.1).

[stalemate is not check, SEALED] In the same position check is FALSE - sealed with claimed = false (sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY). Stalemate needs both: no legal move AND the king not attacked. The second condition is what separates a draw from a mate; the engine seals the negative as a negative.
[the start position is quiet, SEALED] From the initial position White is not in check (claimed = false, sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY).
[and not mated, SEALED] Nor checkmated (claimed = false, sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY): twenty legal moves exist.
[a legal move, SEALED] e2e4 is legal from the start (sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY): a pawn may advance two squares from its starting rank (Laws 3.7.2).

[an illegal move, SEALED AS ILLEGAL] e2e5 is NOT legal - sealed with claimed = false (sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY). Three squares is not a pawn move; the generator lists the twenty legal moves and this is not among them. A miss stays a miss.

[en passant, SEALED] After 1.e4 c5 2.e5 d5 the capture e5xd6 is legal (sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY): a pawn that just advanced two squares may be taken as if it had moved one (Laws 3.7.4.1), on that move only.

[castling, SEALED] In the 'kiwipete' position White may castle kingside, e1g1 (sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY): king and rook unmoved, squares between empty, no square the king crosses attacked (Laws 3.8.2). The position's perft(2) = 2039 is the standard that proves the generator.
[material, SEALED] At the start the material balance is 0 (sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY): both sides hold 8 + 6 + 6 + 10 + 9 = 39 points on the 1/3/3/5/9 scale.
[a pawn up, SEALED] After scholar's mate White is +1 (sealed through chess.CHESS_VERIFY): the f7 pawn was the capture. The count is a convention; the capture is a fact.

[the Laws, CITED] The FIDE Laws of Chess are the postulate set: how each piece moves, check, checkmate, stalemate, en passant, castling. They are chosen rules, cited and never sealed; every verdict above is a theorem of them, computed exhaustively over the legal moves. The piece values 1/3/3/5/9 are a convention of the literature, not a law.
marks.source: FIDE Laws of Chess (2023); the 1/3/3/5/9 scale (standard literature convention)

marks.claim: [the bound, stated] The verifier decides what is TRUE of a position - mate, stalemate, legality, material - by exhaustive legal-move generation, proven by perft (start: 20 / 400 / 8902; kiwipete: 2039 at depth 2). It never plays, evaluates, or recommends a move: what the best move is lies outside the closed set and is declined.

[on the one map] Strategy has three witnesses here: game theory (the abstract equilibrium), the body under pressure (the combat grammar), and chess - the one where perfect information makes optimal literally computable, so it is the calibration rig for the other two. Ties the game-theory stick and card_floor_the_mind; the search tree is card_floor_computer_science.
